meta.board: daily_v5/out/wnba_hybrid_daily.parquet (prior-informed board, in-ridge WNBA box prior, net == sum6)
meta.board_scale: points per 100 possessions, WNBA-only scale (no NBA translation)

board_choice.why_prior_informed: it is the board the site's Explorer and Tables default to, and it predicts games slightly better out of sample: margin RMSE 12.5513 (pure) -> 12.4831 (prior-informed), gain +0.068 with a paired game-clustered 95% CI of [+0.019, +0.118] that excludes zero, positive in all four OOS seasons.
board_choice.honest_limit: the same gain wins only 24 of 42 walk-forward blocks (sign test p=0.44), so it is magnitude-driven, not block-consistent. It is a small edge, not a different model.
board_choice.coupling: the board and priors/wnba_game_model*.json are chosen from ONE key. `a` absorbs the board's scale and the prior-informed board is ~28% wider (sd(net) 1.730 -> 2.217 on the as-of day), so feeding hybrid strengths through the pure board's a=1.1443 over-disperses every margin by ~6.3%.

strength_level.note: team strength is a 5-man on-floor SUM of board net, and the board is a five-season window whose own mean is not 0, so the raw 15-team mean was +4.91. That constant has been SUBTRACTED from every published strength: 0.0 now means an average 2026 WNBA team. Only DIFFERENCES enter the game model, so the shift changes no projection -- the simulation is unchanged by it.
strength_level.raw_level_recoverable: each team also carries strength_uncentred, so a page that wants the board's own level still has it.

centring_invariance.what: same seed, strengths shifted by a common constant; the game model sees only differences, so every simulated margin is bit-identical and so is every derived quantity

game_model.prediction: pred_margin = hca + a*poss_scale*(strength_home - strength_away) + team_err_home - team_err_away;  margin ~ N(pred, sigma_game)
game_model.why_regular_season_block: the pooled hca 1.979 is inflated by 89 playoff games whose home side is the better seed; the seed advantage is modelled explicitly here, so using it would double-count

minutes.expectation: per-player mean minutes over their team's last 10 games, normalized to 200 player-minutes per team per game
minutes.minutes_per_team_game_note: 40-minute game x 5 on the floor. NOT the NBA's 240. It cancels out of team strength (a ratio) but IS the scale of every published exp_mpg.
minutes.window_selected_by: NOT tuned -- the sweep is a documented null, see minutes_window_sweep

availability_sensitivity.what: strength_all_available / proj_wins_all_available rebuild every team on MINUTES-WHEN-AVAILABLE (window minutes / window appearances), renormalized to 200. That redistributes minutes to the intermittently-available starters without inflating anyone; it is an upper bound on 'everybody healthy', not a forecast.
availability_sensitivity.why: there is no WNBA injury or availability feed in this repo, so a return date cannot be modelled. Restoring SEASON averages does not bound it either: a player out all season has a low season average too.
availability_sensitivity.limitation: a player with zero appearances in the window is left out entirely -- they are indistinguishable from one who was traded or released.

minutes_window_sweep.harness: weekly forward cuts 2023-2026, 837 games; rebuild strength from the last K team games and the board day before the cut, predict the next 7 days; RMSE gain vs the season-long window, paired game-clustered bootstrap (4,000 draws)
minutes_window_sweep.verdict: NULL -- every CI crosses 0. Best point estimate K=8 (+0.052 RMSE); the whole K=3..season-long range spans 0.053 RMSE, i.e. less than one fifth of the game-model's own RMSE standard error (0.277).
minutes_window_sweep.cost_of_not_knowing_minutes: 0.05 RMSE. Same 758-game subset, the realised-minutes oracle (workstream C's construction, which knows who actually played) scores 12.4939 against 12.5454 for the K=8 projection. Much smaller than C's flat-5-man penalty of 0.22, which measured a different thing (no minute weighting at all, rather than projected weights).

factor_profile.construction: per team, F_f = 5 * sum(exp_mpg_p * f_p) / sum(exp_mpg_p) -- the same minute-weighted 5-man on-floor construction as strength, on the same board day. net == sum6, so a team's six factor values sum to its UNCENTRED strength and its six DEVIATIONS from the league average sum to its CENTRED strength.
factor_profile.sign_convention: all six are sign-aligned so higher is better, defence included (dTS positive = suppressing opponent efficiency).
factor_profile.band_is: the middle 80% (10th-90th percentile) of the 15 TEAMS' deviations on that factor -- a league SPREAD, i.e. how ordinary a bar of that length is. It is not an uncertainty interval.
factor_profile.se_is: factors_se is an UNCERTAINTY, not a spread: the board's own per-player standard errors propagated through the minute shares as se_F = 5*sqrt(sum(share_p^2 * se_p^2)).
factor_profile.se_is_an_upper_bound: that propagation assumes teammates' estimates are INDEPENDENT. They are not: the ridge design is collinear across teammates, so their posterior covariance is negative and a team aggregate is better identified than any member of it. Dropping that term makes this number too WIDE. By how much is not measurable from what is on disk (only the per-player diagonal is stored), so it is published as a conservative bound. It is typically LARGER than the league sd of the same factor -- do not draw it as the visual spread; use `band` for that.
factor_profile.se_minor_bias_the_other_way: off-board players are imputed at 0 with SE 0, which omits their share of the uncertainty. That share is small: see roster_links.unlinkable_minute_share and each team's board_minute_coverage.
factor_profile.per_player: each roster row carries f[0..5] and f_se[0..5] in the FAC6 order, on the RAW board scale (not multiplied by 5, not centred), so a page can rebuild the team profile itself.

roster_links.id_scheme: gid = 'w' + the stats.nba PERSON_ID, i.e. the same global id the Explorer and the Tables page key on.
roster_links.why_unlinkable: build_wnba_site.py only publishes a player page for a player who clears its own gate (peak weighted exposure >= 300 AND >= 10 board days). Every unlinkable row here is a deep-bench player who fails it -- the largest is 6.0 expected mpg. Four of them are not on the board at all (on_board=false, imputed at 0). Render the name as plain text; do not link it.

schedule.strength_of_schedule: each team's remaining schedule.sos is the mean PUBLISHED (centred) strength of its remaining opponents, so positive = harder than average. Home-court is not folded in; the home/away split and per-side SOS are separate. sos_rank 1 = hardest remaining slate.

gap_2026_07_23_to_07_27.verdict: no regular-season coverage gap: the only fixture between the board's last day and the schedule's next game is the All-Star game, which is excluded

schedule.nickname_map_source: DERIVED from the 201 played 2026 games (schedule nickname vs PBP location+teamtricode); home and away routes agree and each nickname resolves to one tricode

recovered_from_full.note: Game 1022600052 (2026-05-27, PDX 71 - CON 61) is dropped by the source package's CONSERVATIVE lineup-validation step, not missing from the package: the full normalized play-by-play carries all four periods and a complete score, and the Clean surface removes exactly its 507 rows. A W-L record needs a final score and nothing else, so the result is counted in the standings here while the game stays out of the RAPM solve, where the lineup failure genuinely disqualifies it. An earlier build said it was 'absent at every stage' and published PDX at 10-16; that was wrong.

playoff_format.assumed: ASSUMED for 2026 = the 2025 format, verified from the 2025 data: an 8-team field seeded 1-8 league-wide with no conference split; round 1 best-of-3 (home hi-lo-hi); semifinals best-of-5 (home hi-hi-lo-lo-hi) in a FIXED bracket (1/8 vs 4/5, 2/7 vs 3/6, no reseeding); final best-of-7 (home hi-hi-lo-lo-hi-lo-hi). Not verifiable for 2026: the league has not published a 2026 bracket in this data and 2026 is an expansion year (15 teams), so an 8-team field is an assumption, as is the home pattern of finals games 5-7 (the 2025 final was a sweep).
playoff_format.semifinal_pairs: winner(1v8) vs winner(4v5); winner(2v7) vs winner(3v6)
playoff_format.seeding: win percentage, ties broken by total point differential (the league uses head-to-head; PD is a proxy)

verified_against_2025.source: 2025 playoffs (WNBA25_PS.csv) vs 2025 regular-season standings derived here
verified_against_2025.note: the final ended 4-0, and only a best-of-7 admits a 4-win series, so the best-of-7 length is measured rather than assumed. What a sweep CANNOT reveal is the home pattern of games 5-7; that part of FINAL['home'] is the league's standard 2-2-1-1-1 and is assumed. Where the reproducing seeding and my derived one disagree, the cause is the 3 of 310 games the 2025 corpus lacks plus the league's head-to-head tiebreak, which this repo has no feed for -- a standings question, not a format question.

score_derivation.route: max of the running home_score/away_score within a game_id, from the collaborator normalized PBP; team identity from location+teamtricode on the same rows

caveats: No external benchmark exists for the WNBA — no closing line, no rival metric. Every number here is internal to this pipeline.

There is no WNBA injury or availability feed. A player who has missed their team's last 10 games has an expected ~0 minutes here even if they are about to return; a player who just went down still carries their recent minutes. The loudest live case is MIN's Napheesa Collier, who played exactly ONE 2026 game (2026-07-22, 22.2 min) and so enters at 2.2 expected mpg. An ‘if everyone were available’ rebuild is reported alongside, and each team page carries its own minutes watchlist.
Team strength is frozen at the 2026-07-22 board and does not drift, improve or age over the remaining 8 weeks. Only the measured persistent rating error is resampled.
The persistent-team-error variance is itself estimated from 52 team-seasons, so the width of the win-total bands carries real estimation error.
Roster moves after 2026-07-22 (trades, signings, waivers) are invisible.
The playoff bracket for 2026 is assumed, not published — the assumed bracket is stated above.

The prior-informed board is used because it is the site's default basis and it predicts games marginally better (12.5513 -> 12.4831 OOS margin RMSE, CI excluding zero). It wins only 24 of 42 walk-forward blocks, so that edge is magnitude-driven, not consistent. Switching back to the pure board moves no team's projected wins by more than 0.4 and does not change the standings order or the favourite — the board comparison is on the Model page.

Strength is CENTRED on the 15-team mean, so 0.0 is an average 2026 team. The shift is simulation-invariant — the whole simulation is bit-identical with and without it — but it is a shift of a five-season board's level onto a one-season league, not a re-solve: a player's own net on the Explorer is still on the board's raw scale.
